✅ Learning

Accuracy

In simple words

The share of examples a model gets right, usually measured on a test set.

The percentage of answers a model gets right. It's a useful first number, but it can mislead: if 95 of 100 leaves are healthy, a model that always says “healthy” is 95% accurate and still useless. So people also look at which mistakes a model makes.

Example. A spam filter that sorts 970 of 1,000 test emails correctly has 97% accuracy.

Related words

  • Test setExamples put aside before training and used only to check how well a model does on data it has never seen.
  • False positiveA false alarm: the model says “yes” (spam, sick, danger) when the true answer is “no”.
